rounds.notes:
First round... obviously we go for [Clone Conjuration](item_6c9f6be1-ab29-4f46-af24-34e4835f9af3) !

Even though in the first round you won’t be able to fully unleash the devastating potential of this ability, cloning yourself will still grant you extra healing and damage depending on the situation.

As core abilities, we pick [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0) + [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf), while the third one can be adapted depending on your opponents and the playstyle you want to adopt in this opening phase.

**If you prefer a more aggressive approach**, go for [Plasma Converter](item_25869f9a-9a29-4e19-96b6-9d8a28c59318). 

*Personally, I prefer this because it helps us sustain ourselves while attacking enemies between heals. This not only helps your team secure kills, but also lets you earn more points.
However, remember that to be a good Kiriko balancing damage and healing is essential.
If your teammates are struggling, don’t get stubborn about landing hits—help them!
There are plenty of opportunities to secure kills or deal lethal damage to enemies—
you don’t need to sacrifice your team’s life for it.
Having one or more teammates down puts your team at a serious disadvantage—don’t forget that!*

**If you’re up against heroes you’re not comfortable handling,** choose [Armored Vest](item_358361e2-59be-4c81-b221-8a87f37809e6) or [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da) . These powers will give you a decent chance of survival.


There are two other options that might work well for you:

The first one is [Power Playbook](item_6d8803cf-baa7-46ee-af91-51e7f2301418), which allows you to slightly enhance your [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568);

The second is [Charged Plating](item_b8ca58e7-6ae2-40ee-8618-fe2f32315295), often underestimated, but for heroes like Kiriko ( who tend to charge their ultimate fairly quickly ) choosing a power that grants 10 base health, but after using your [Kitsune Rush](ability_67ce89b9-6410-415c-bc87-70dbdb19d71c) it gives u 25 armor and 10% [Ability Power](stat_ability_power) for the rest of the round — making it a highly optimal choice.

*Obviously, only go for this second option if you’re confident in your ability to build up your ultimate quickly, otherwise, you risk wasting those points.
An experienced Kiriko player will have no doubts about its potential, but if you’re just starting out, stick to one of the previously mentioned abilities for a safer choice.*


In every build, I tend to give this piece of advice, which reflects the flexibility of the options listed here:
It's always better to choose options that highlight your playstyle. Some abilities are obviously key for the core functionality of the suggested build — but that doesn’t mean you can’t customize the rest!

Second Round: We’ve got one job: buy [Donut Delivery](item_296adb69-d517-4885-903a-ef8f3a1d6a7b) .

No doubts. No second thoughts. No hesitation.
This is a mandatory ability.

Not enough points?
Sell all your greens.

Still short on points after selling all your greens?
Highly unlikely. Seriously, I find that hard to believe.

But hey, I’ll give you the benefit of the doubt—maybe you’re in one of those games where, thanks to you or teammates who seem like they just finished the tutorial, everything’s falling apart and you’re this close to uninstalling.

Don’t give up — not yet.

We’re only approaching the second round, and there’s still time to turn things around.
My recommendation: buy [Icy Coolant](item_8b1c21e9-33e8-49a6-8277-a3a06d55a65f).
It costs just 5,500 points and gives you 10% [Weapon Power](stat_weapon_power) plus a 5% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction), which definitely helps with both [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568) and [Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014).
If you happen to have a few points left, go for some greens.


If you’ve reached the point where you can’t earn enough points because your teammates keep dying randomly or decide it’s a great idea to push 1v5, try to communicate with them. And when the game allows it, don’t be afraid to be a little selfish.

Your individual scaling might just be what carries the team to victory.

At this point, the obvious choice becomes [Two-Zu](item_80f16d3e-a4c0-4fa8-90b1-a0f033a1a77b). Why?
Well… obvious.

[Kiriko](hero_70a0ac5c-2a55-4fab-beeb-2f570886426f) is annoying (in the best way) thanks to her ability to cancel out most negative effects and this power lets you make your target invulnerable for a few moments.
Need I say more?

With this power unlocked, our goal now becomes clear:
From here on out, we want to further enhance our abilities.
The combo of [Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014) and  [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568) will require our full attention.
In our ability slots, we now want to add [Iridescent Iris](item_b7fb28ef-ce82-416b-8693-01c274f8df4e):

+20% [Ability Power](stat_ability_power)
+10% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction)
Plus, after using your ultimate, you gain 3 seconds of Overhealth —
not essential, but definitely a nice bonus.

If it's a bit too expensive for your current economy, don’t worry — we’ve got some solid alternatives:

[Multi-tool](item_5ba8d94e-f2f3-44b7-8773-025fc6ed7c56)→ gives you a nerfed version of the ability you’re skipping;

[Ironclad Exhaust Ports](item_2d085fa5-ace6-4fab-9323-b7a06268bcd0) → cooldown reduction plus survivability, a solid hybrid choice;

[Icy Coolant](item_8b1c21e9-33e8-49a6-8277-a3a06d55a65f) → still gives you [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction), plus a bit of weapon power, which never hurts.

In case you haven’t figured it out yet,
our top priority is to stack [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction) like it’s raining.

Round 4: the ideal setup at this point should look like the one shown here on the side.
Ideally, you’ll have reached 25% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction) which makes healing a breeze just by using [Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014) .

We’re not quite at the stage where the enemy team is rage-quitting in despair but we’re annoying enough to draw a whole lot of attention.

Taking you down will become their life mission.
Let them try — it’s up to you to fully leverage Kiriko’s potential to make sure they fail.

My advice:
Make the most out of your cooldowns and wall-climb ability.
If you get reckless, you might not have your escape tools available when you need them most.

We’re not at the point where you can just turn your brain off and teleport into chaos,
but we’re getting close — so keep using these rounds to bait, dodge, and vanish just in time to save your teammates.

There’s no doubt: [Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014) is a massive heal, it brings players back from the brink of death. And let’s be honest, sometimes you’ll also need a well-timed [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568) to guarantee a safe reset and turn the fight into a checkmate on the battlefield.

It’s time to unlock our third power — and here’s where the fun begins.

A whole range of possibilities opens up, and I’ll give you three strong options, each tailored to a different kind of scenario.

[Cleansing Charge](item_4721f307-30d2-4fc1-a10b-6de7141deb68)
One of the most popular powers — and the one I personally choose almost every time.
By cleansing anti-healing, bleeds, stuns, and damage-over-time effects, you’ll be able to ult more often during the round and we all know how devastating Kiriko’s [Kitsune Rush](ability_67ce89b9-6410-415c-bc87-70dbdb19d71c) can be.
This power works particularly well against heroes like [Junker Queen](hero_4794d288-27d9-49e0-a1dd-ffe0f4de3ab1), [Ana](hero_f1aee6cf-704f-455f-a100-ec882ebbe000), [Ashe](hero_37b42a2d-a82d-4a22-9df2-4c812c873b54) or even [Moira](hero_7fb6ff1e-a193-40c0-bd0a-25c1928fbaed), who often relies on anti-heal builds.
Obviously, the more you can cleanse, the more valuable this power becomes — and your choice will be pretty clear at that point.

[Leaf On The Wind](item_b64de259-d122-407d-a7e4-9d7267310704)
A solid pick if you need stronger healing output.
While [Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014) will be your main source of healing, there are games where you’ll really feel the pressure.
This usually happens when your second support has decided to go full DPS, or when the enemy team is playing super well and you’re sweating bullets just to keep your team afloat.

[Triple Threat](item_fc0e3d9a-5315-41c2-9aa4-331becace714)
This is my go-to when [Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014) healing is enough or when the other support is healing just as much (or more) than I am.
It allows you to play a more aggressive style, and throwing extra kunai using your main healing ability becomes a fun little bonus 😄


No matter which of these three you pick, your ability slots won’t change because our power level is about to skyrocket.

With [Hardlight Accelerator](item_0390c8af-2a68-4da2-b876-93da32c3f448), here’s what you’re getting:
+10% [Weapon Power](stat_weapon_power)
+10% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction)
And each time you use an ability, you gain +5% [Weapon Power](stat_weapon_power) for 3 seconds, stacking up to 3 times.

Do the math:
[Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014) + [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568) already gives you a 10% bonus.
Once you’ve stacked enough [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction) to use your abilities without even thinking, you’re looking at a guaranteed +15% [Weapon Power](stat_weapon_power) boost, which definitely doesn’t hurt when you’re out there throwing lethal kunai at enemies.

With the current setup (as illustrated), you'll be sitting at 35% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction).

If you’ve got extra points burning a hole in your pocket, here’s what I recommend:
[Icy Coolant](item_8b1c21e9-33e8-49a6-8277-a3a06d55a65f) → brings you up to 40%
[Martian Mender](item_0099632b-4e18-450e-844f-22c40e51bc98) → if you’re filthy rich, go all in — this will take you straight to 45% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction)!

If you haven’t done it yet, it’s time to pick up [Martian Mender](item_0099632b-4e18-450e-844f-22c40e51bc98).
As mentioned in the previous round, this ability grants you an additional +10% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction) and +25 Health.
On top of that, you regenerate 3% of your HP per second, not exactly essential for a ninja-style build like this, but hey, it doesn’t hurt!


If you already picked it up, you’ve now got two options:

1. Stick with your current build, maintaining a total of 45% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction).

2. Drop [Ironclad Exhaust Ports](item_2d085fa5-ace6-4fab-9323-b7a06268bcd0), losing 5% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction), and invest in a different power spike for this build.

Before going into more detail on option 2, let me point something out:
Testing different setups in the Practice Range, I noticed that dropping from 45% to 40% [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction) doesn’t feel like a big difference.

So, if you’re sitting on a mountain of points like Scrooge McDuck, I strongly suggest taking a good look at the following two upgrades:

For more personal survivability:
[Goddess's Aura](item_a36d46c8-cee0-4c97-b6e4-72bb816c13dc) gives you:
+25 Health
+100 Overhealth every time you use [Swift Step](ability_7f6c99f6-7a6f-4f67-a8fd-d6bf6a09e014)
This significantly boosts your survivability, and let's be honest —
you'll start collecting hate from the enemy team like never before.

For stronger team survivability:
[Talisman of Life](item_7ecfd3eb-d869-41fe-87eb-0bb2e82e5718) enhances your [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568) by giving +80 Overhealth for 5 seconds to your allies.
With your current [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction) and the number of [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568) at your disposal by  [Two-Zu](item_80f16d3e-a4c0-4fa8-90b1-a0f033a1a77b), this power becomes incredibly useful, especially in the final rounds.

Why?

Because just like you, your enemies will now be extremely dangerous too, and giving your team an edge like this is not to be underestimated.

One important thing to clarify about its potential:
You have two [Protection Suzu](ability_e0d6579f-d70a-4a5e-a58d-aee40d00c568).
If you spam both of them back-to-back — like many players do — you’ll end up waiting 8 seconds to cast one again.
But spacing them out even slightly reduces the downtime significantly, creating a sense of continuity and maximizing the overall benefit.

Here we are — the final round.

Once again, I’m putting you in front of an informed decision that will ultimately define what kind of Kiriko you want to be.

As you may have noticed, I’ve added [Keen Kunai](item_d5993121-8a5f-4c59-9145-19dc55265f48) to the equation.

Why?

Because if, in this round or the previous one, you decide to drop both remaining rare abilities namely [Ironclad Exhaust Ports](item_2d085fa5-ace6-4fab-9323-b7a06268bcd0)and [Multi-tool](item_5ba8d94e-f2f3-44b7-8773-025fc6ed7c56)
you’ll end up with 10% less [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction).

Now, hear me out:
That 10% equals roughly one extra second,
and honestly, when you're picking up strong powers like [Talisman of Life](item_7ecfd3eb-d869-41fe-87eb-0bb2e82e5718) and [Goddess's Aura](item_a36d46c8-cee0-4c97-b6e4-72bb816c13dc), that trade-off makes sense.

Let’s say it plainly — the benefits of that combo are so strong that losing one second of cooldown probably won’t make or break you.

However, if your aim is sharp and you’re a true [Kiriko](hero_70a0ac5c-2a55-4fab-beeb-2f570886426f) main, then I strongly recommend giving [Keen Kunai](item_d5993121-8a5f-4c59-9145-19dc55265f48) a serious look.

Why?

Because every critical hit landed will grant [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction), and if you’ve chosen an aggressive playstyle, or plan to switch to one in the final round, this ability can make your gameplay both highly effective and incredibly fun, all while maintaining the core advantages this build is built on.

Alternatively, you can pick one of the two powers you left aside back in Round 5.
And yes, I know I’m being repetitive here, but I’m going to list their benefits again so you don’t have to scroll back and forth.
I get it — most of the time, we check online builds while playing, and if you’re not already familiar with every detail, you don’t exactly have time to spare.
So, if that’s not your case, forgive me — but I need to consider everyone’s needs if I really want to be helpful 😄

As for the powers:
The same principle I mentioned at the beginning still applies: It’s up to you whether to sacrifice your blue abilities and go full purple or keep things humble and stick to your current setup.
Of course, I’ve left a hybrid on the side, just in case you’re short on points or simply prefer a middle-ground approach.
 often go full purple myself, so feel free to choose whatever u like and have fun 😄
